title: Perceived business benefits of workforce diversity can rise across parties while DEI performance judgments remain divided
source_unit: Bentley University-Gallup Business in Society survey reporting

denominator.unit: percent of U.S. adults in the Bentley University-Gallup Business in Society survey

diverse_workforces_more_profitable.unit: percent saying it is somewhat or completely true that businesses with diverse workforces are more profitable

diverse_workforces_more_innovative.unit: percent saying businesses with diverse workforces make more innovative products

dei_business_priority.unit: percent saying promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion is a somewhat or extremely important business priority

business_dei_performance_good_or_excelle.unit: percent rating businesses good or excellent at promoting DEI

profitability_democrats.unit: percent of Democrats saying diverse workforces are more profitable

observations.method: Bentley University-Gallup Business in Society survey reporting; the source compares public judgments about business outcomes, priorities, and business performance by party.
observations.uncertainty: These are perceptions and priorities, not firm-level profitability, innovation, workforce composition, employee experience, or causal effects of diversity practices. The release summary does not provide a same-respondent link from belief to workplace exposure or firm behavior.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults by party identification; party differences may overlap with ideology, workplace exposure, information, industry, and question framing.
observations.counterinterpretation: People may believe diversity improves business performance while opposing particular DEI programs, distrusting firm implementation, or having no direct workplace exposure. A performance rating is not a measure of actual firm practice.

related_sources.claim: Gallup's corruption-perception release provides a complementary public-legitimacy and institutional-trust comparison.

boundary: This record establishes a current survey pattern in how Americans judge workforce diversity and business performance. It does not establish actual firm outcomes, employee treatment, causal diversity effects, or durable political consensus.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Gallup article page retrieved and URL hash recorded; respondent microdata and full survey file are not retained
